sites.rationale: The construct name 'Myc-IGSF1-HA' follows the standard convention of placing the leading tag at the N-terminus. IGSF1 carries a signal peptide (residues 1–28, last residue G28); a tag inserted upstream of residue 29 would be cleaved with the SP, so the functional junction is after G28 (insert_after_residue=28), placing the Myc tag at the extracellular mature N-terminus (EC1 spans 29–518, >490 residues from TM1). Python confirmed residue 28 = G and residue 29 = M. No explicit residue number is given in the ledger clip, so position_evidence is topology_derived; IGSF1 has exactly one extracellular N-terminus, leaving no ambiguity. Full-length human IGSF1 expressed in heterologous cells as a dual-tagged construct named Myc-IGSF1-HA (PMC3511587). The Myc prefix in the construct name places the tag at the protein N-terminus; with a signal peptide spanning residues 1–28, the tag must reside between the SP cleavage site and the mature N-terminus (junction 28/29) to survive to the cell surface. The paper used this construct to study IGSF1 trafficking and cell-surface expression.

literature_notes: The ledger contains only one clip (L1) for IGSF1, reporting a dual Myc-IGSF1-HA construct used to study trafficking and cell-surface expression (PMC3511587). The Myc tag is placed at the extracellular N-terminus (after SP cleavage, junction G28/M29) and qualifies as a surface site. The HA tag, implied by the '-HA' suffix, is at the protein C-terminus (residue 1336), which falls in the intracellular span (1282–1336) and is recorded in other_positions. No residue number is given in the clip for either tag, so both positions are topology-derived. No internal loop insertions, transposon screens, or additional tagged constructs are present in the ledger for IGSF1, so only one surface site is reported.

literature_other_positions.note: HA tag at the C-terminus of the Myc-IGSF1-HA construct; residue 1336 (I) falls within the intracellular C-terminal span (1282–1336), making this tag cytoplasmic and not suitable for extracellular surface labelling.
